analyst_view.overall: Early view: Two mid-table sides with no European games. De Rossi's Genoa had won three in a row before losing 2-1 to Milan, a game in which they out-shot Milan 17-6, and they have an almost full squad. Torino are mid-table under Abate, struggle in the final third, and had injuries to Ricardo Rodriguez and Fortini before the break.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Genoa's home games have averaged about 2.5 goals and Torino's away games about 2.6, so the number fits. Both attacks have been blunt, so I see no reason to move.

corners.text: The site expects 8.7 corners. I lean slightly higher: Genoa's home games have averaged over ten corners, and Torino's away games almost nine. Genoa attack the wings at home with Ellertsson now playing mainly as a wide player.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. I lean lower because Torino's games have averaged only about 2.2 cards, the fewest in Serie A. Genoa's home games are a little above that, which keeps the lean small.

shots.text: The site expects 25.0 shots. I lean higher: Genoa's home games have averaged almost 29 shots, with opponents shooting freely, and Torino's away games about 28. De Rossi has also told Ellertsson to shoot more.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.5 shots on target. I lean slightly higher, as Torino's away games have averaged over nine on target and Genoa's home games about eight. Neither side is accurate, so this is a small lean.
